title: CHAPTER 23: ECONOMIC REFORMS IN INDIA (1991 – LPG MODEL)

blocks.content: INTRODUCTION TO ECONOMIC REFORMS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Economic Reforms were introduced in 1991 to transform India from a closed, regulated economy to a strong, competitive, and globally connected system.
The reforms were triggered by a severe Balance of Payments crisis, high fiscal deficit, rapid inflation, heavy external debt, and foreign reserves lasting only 2 weeks.
Financial assistance was secured from the IMF and World Bank under conditions of economic deregulation, trade liberalisation, and reduction of subsidies.
The LPG Model consists of Liberalisation (removing government controls), Privatisation (transferring public enterprises to private ownership), and Globalisation (integrating with the world economy).
Major achievements include high GDP growth, increased FDI, and service sector expansion, alongside challenges like job insecurity and income inequality.

BACKGROUND OF ECONOMIC REFORMS (WHY 1991 REFORMS WERE NEEDED)
By 1990–91, India faced a severe economic crisis due to:
India had very low foreign exchange reserves (only enough for 2 weeks of imports).
Government expenditure was very high compared to income.
Prices of essential goods were rising rapidly.
Industries were inefficient due to government control.
India had borrowed heavily from foreign countries.
Oil prices increased and remittances decreased.
Due to these reasons, India had no option but to reform its economy.

Economic Reforms of 1991 changed the face of Indian economy.
LPG MODEL OF ECONOMIC REFORMS
Economic Reforms of 1991 are based on three major pillars:
L – Liberalisation P – Privatisation G – Globalisation
Together, they are called LPG Reforms.

Foreign exchange reserves in 1991 had depleted to cover only 2 weeks of imports, making it a key trigger for BoP crisis questions.
Reforms were implemented under structural adjustment program conditions stipulated by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
The New Industrial Policy of 1991 abolished the License Raj (industrial licensing) and reduced public sector monopoly.
Privatisation methods frequently tested include Disinvestment, Outsourcing, and Public-Private Partnerships (PPP).

CONCLUSION

Economic Reforms of 1991 changed the face of Indian economy. They helped India move from a closed economy to a global economy. Though challenges exist, LPG reforms have played a major role in making India one of the fastest growing economies in the world.
